## Summary

This page presents an inventory snapshot of scalars, lists, and maps in chart defaults, checked-in overlays, GitOps values and manifests, release values, and infrastructure manifests. Open a file section to inspect its nested fields. The inventory redacts credentials, identities, and access lists. A redacted value remains configurable, but this page never publishes its content.

## Select And Verify A Change

1. Find the owning file below. Chart values are defaults; a checked-in overlay is not automatically selected by every command.
2. Read the receiving source and precedence column. Direct deploy uses generated release values and its optional selected overlay. Production GitOps selects immutable bundle resources through its Application source.
3. Change the owning input, not a generated release copy alone. Render the selected chart or regenerate the bundle through the linked producer. Inspect the affected workload, Secret reference and policy before applying it.
4. After the normal deployment, verify the effective resource and process health. Source discovery and rendering do not prove a rollout, API admission, image behavior or cluster policy enforcement.

Scope: all YAML inputs currently discovered under charts, examples, gitops, my-values and releases/values. The file index records the actual selected membership, not a fixed count. Nested API contracts explain the selected manifest fields; this bounded values reference does not renew unrelated global program-output, environment or CI-purpose qualifications. Secret and access-list contents remain redacted. Unsupported or image-owned boundaries are stated in their rows.

| `$.busterNamespaceBroker.allowedPrefixes` | Defines the namespace-name prefixes shared by the namespace controller, its admission fence, and the namespace-lease CRD. Accepted values: Use a deliberate nonempty list of valid namespace-name prefixes, such as &#91;&#34;test&#34;&#93;. The controller matches prefix plus &#34;-&#34;; the CRD enum restricts spec.namespacePrefix when that optional field is supplied. Selected chart default: the checked-in value in this row is the chart default. Empty or omitted value: Omission keeps the earlier list; a later &#91;&#93; replaces it with no items. All three templates render only when busterNamespaceBroker.enabled is true and agentRole is buster; the fence also requires Kubernetes &#62;=1.30. An omitted override retains the merged list. An effective &#91;&#93; renders an empty controller environment string, &#91;&#93;.exists(prefix, ...) in the Fail/Deny fence, and enum: &#91;&#93; in the lease CRD. The controller falls back to test and the fence cannot match any namespace name. The CRD renders enum: &#91;&#93;, but the pinned Kubernetes validator checks enum values only when that list is nonempty, so this empty enum adds no restriction on namespacePrefix; the remaining schema and admission rules still apply. Validator proof: &#91;CRD enum conversion&#93;(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66452049f3d692768c39c797b21b793dce80314e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/validation/validation.go#L293-L298), &#91;enum consumer&#93;(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66452049f3d692768c39c797b21b793dce80314e/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/schema.go#L197-L203), and &#91;nonempty-enum validation&#93;(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66452049f3d692768c39c797b21b793dce80314e/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/validator.go#L56-L71). Explicit null renders null.exists(prefix, ...) and a null enum; neither template uses the controller fallback. Null is not a supported recovery value. | `$.spec.syncPolicy.retry` | Configures retries of failed or errored sync operations. Accepted values: The pinned authority (argo-cd@10.8.0 rendered CRDs) defines type &#96;object&#96; for the exact field &#96;spec.syncPolicy.retry&#96;. Operational constraint: The exact field, item and child schema contracts listed here apply together. Default: The exact field schema defines no default. Omission: The parent schema permits omission. The exact field schema defines no default. Collection result: In a fresh typed Application, omission or null leaves retry nil; an empty object creates a strategy with limit zero, backoff nil and refresh false. ## Illustrative Values That Require Preparation

[examples/buster-values.yaml](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ce8f291f59a2752bd2f231a539a139ea689ae8e2/examples/buster-values.yaml#L1-L1) is an illustrative input. Its unchanged standalone render stops with <code>Error: execution error at (kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:1593:12): Buster registry configuration requires exactly one extraContainers entry named buster-v2-runtime</code>. No resource is emitted.

Do not deploy this illustrative file alone. The chart rejects it before any Kubernetes resource is emitted. Prepare complete Buster values with exactly one buster-v2-runtime container and configured node-reachable registry transport and credentials, then require successful bound offline rendering before deployment. The runtime deploy path additionally requires a verified selected runtime release materialization; no release receipt is fabricated. Owner: platform operator preparing agent values. Follow [configuration preparation](../use/install.md#select-configuration).

This current reference covers the checked-in Helm and GitOps values listed above. It does not regenerate or qualify the separate inventory of programmatic API producers. For a selected value's receiving API, use its field explanation, pinned authority and collection contract below.

## Runtime Meaning

| Value group | Runtime effect | Expected proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| image and pull secrets | selects agent and sidecar images, tags, pull policy, and GHCR pull Secret | rendered Deployments include expected image refs and `imagePullSecrets` |
| auth/provider/Discord/Stitch/LiteLLM | selects direct values or existing Secret name/key references | rendered env refs point to expected Secret keys and generated secrets reference lists those keys |
| persistence | creates workspace/config PVCs for gateway and plugin-runtime state | rendered PVCs and security contexts match production values |
| service and extra ports | exposes gateway/bridge ClusterIP ports plus explicit extra NodePorts | rendered Services contain only documented ports |
| buster namespace broker | adds lease CRD/RBAC/controller and controller env vars | Buster render includes CRD, lease client RBAC, controller Deployment, and namespace fence docs |
| probes, startup doctor, and dependency checks | configures gateway, Redis, and LiteLLM health checks; `gateway.startupDoctor` runs `openclaw doctor --fix` as a blocking state update while the gateway is stopped | rendered init container, env vars, and smoke commands exercise the health and doctor surfaces |

## Failure Signals

- A top-level value appears in this page but has no rendered effect: add deployment truth coverage or remove the stale value.
- Rendered Secret refs do not match `my-values/setup-secrets.sh`: update values, helper, inventory, and docs together.
- Buster values disable sandbox/broker behavior unexpectedly: inspect `my-values/buster-values.yaml` before changing chart templates.
- A live pod keeps old config after values change: remember the init container preserves persisted config unless override flags request replacement.
